nodes.title: README Purpose
nodes.summary: State the product audience, problem, supported use cases, and non-goals at the top of the README. This lets prospective users judge fit before installation and avoids unsupported adoption.
nodes.probe: Inspect the first screen of the README and verify that audience, problem, supported use cases, and non-goals are explicit, mutually consistent, and linked to current documentation.

nodes.title: README Quickstart
nodes.summary: Provide a copy-paste path from a clean checkout or install to one observable successful result. A reproducible first run supports evaluation, onboarding, and incident reproduction.
nodes.probe: In a clean temporary checkout, execute only the README quickstart commands and assert they exit zero and produce the documented result or URL; fail if the documented result is absent.

nodes.title: README Prerequisites
nodes.summary: Document supported operating systems, runtimes, package managers, services, credentials, and minimum versions before setup. Explicit prerequisites distinguish unsupported environments from product defects.
nodes.probe: Compare README prerequisites with runtime manifests, lockfiles, CI images, container configuration, and integration setup; verify every required dependency has a supported version range and credential requirement and no setup command relies on an unstated service.

nodes.title: README Configuration
nodes.summary: Document every required or behavior-changing configuration value with type, default, example, secret handling, and reload semantics. This makes operational changes predictable and prevents unsafe undocumented settings.
nodes.probe: Inventory configuration reads and schemas, compare them with the reference, and check every entry for type, default, example, secret, reload, precedence, and validation information, including unknown and unsafe-value behavior.

nodes.title: Devcontainer Reproducibility
nodes.summary: Declare a reproducible contributor environment that installs project tools and dependencies and exposes the documented workflows. This prevents laptop-specific runtime and system-library drift.
nodes.probe: Run `devcontainer build --workspace-folder .`; `devcontainer up --workspace-folder .`; `devcontainer exec --workspace-folder . <documented-setup>`; and `devcontainer exec --workspace-folder . <documented-version-check>`; assert each exits zero and declared versions match the manifest.

nodes.title: Make Entrypoints
nodes.summary: Provide a small, discoverable, deterministic interface for setup, test, lint, docs, run, and clean operations. Shared task entrypoints keep local, CI, and support workflows consistent.
nodes.probe: In an isolated checkout, run `make -n` for setup, test, lint, docs, and run, then execute each target with documented prerequisites; assert expected exit status and artifacts and verify clean removes only generated artifacts.

nodes.title: Local Parity
nodes.summary: Record which local services, versions, flags, fixtures, and data-loading steps match production and explain accepted differences. Explicit boundaries show what confidence local testing provides.
nodes.probe: Compare the parity matrix with deployment manifests, local compose or devcontainer configuration, feature-flag defaults, fixtures, and staging setup; list every material mismatch with an explicit risk and validation boundary.

nodes.title: Onboarding Path
nodes.summary: Maintain the shortest rehearsed path from clone through setup to a first meaningful reviewable change in less than one working day. This exposes undocumented dependencies and reduces tribal-knowledge bottlenecks.
nodes.probe: Inspect a recent onboarding rehearsal record and follow the documented path in a clean environment, verifying it reaches a meaningful change and review-ready checks within the stated time objective without private oral instructions.

nodes.title: Troubleshooting Guide
nodes.summary: Map common setup and runtime symptoms to diagnostic commands, likely causes, safe fixes, and escalation. This reduces repeated support work and unsafe trial-and-error remediation.
nodes.probe: Select the top recurring failures, follow each guide from symptom through verification, and confirm commands are safe, causes are plausible, fixes are current, evidence is specified, and escalation resolves to an owned channel.

nodes.title: Architecture Overview
nodes.summary: Explain major components, ownership boundaries, data flows, external dependencies, and trust boundaries for design and incident work. Current system context prevents hidden coupling and misrouted response.
nodes.probe: Trace representative user and operational flows through the diagram and code or deployment manifests, checking that components, owners, external dependencies, data stores, and process, tenant, privilege, and network trust boundaries are present and current.

nodes.title: Architecture Source
nodes.summary: Store architecture diagrams as editable reviewable source beside code and render them deterministically with ownership and review metadata. This keeps structural documentation reproducible and maintainable.
nodes.probe: Run the documented diagram render command; compare generated output with checked-in artifacts; assert source files, pinned renderer version, owner metadata, and `last_reviewed` signal exist; fail on render errors or artifact drift.

nodes.title: ADR Records
nodes.summary: Capture consequential architectural decisions with context, decision, alternatives, consequences, owner, date, and status. Durable rationale prevents rejected designs and constraints from being rediscovered or removed accidentally.
nodes.probe: Sample consequential changes and verify each has a linked ADR or explicit reviewable exemption, with all required fields populated and alternatives and consequences specific enough to guide future work.

nodes.title: ADR Lifecycle
nodes.summary: Distinguish proposed, accepted, superseded, and deprecated ADRs and link both sides of each supersession. This keeps obsolete decisions from appearing authoritative.
nodes.probe: Parse ADR status and supersession links; for every superseded or deprecated ADR, verify the replacement exists and both records link the relationship; assert statuses are from the allowed set.

nodes.title: Rationale Comments
nodes.summary: Use inline comments for non-obvious rationale, invariants, compatibility constraints, and rejected alternatives rather than narrating evident code. Preserved reasoning prevents future simplifications from reintroducing defects.
nodes.probe: Sample comments around compatibility branches, invariants, workarounds, and rejected alternatives; verify each explains why the code must be shaped that way, points to evidence where appropriate, and does not duplicate implementation.

nodes.title: OpenAPI Contract
nodes.summary: Publish a complete versioned OpenAPI description of supported HTTP operations, schemas, authentication, errors, and examples. A retrievable exact contract prevents clients from reverse-engineering implementation behavior.
nodes.probe: Validate the OpenAPI document with an OAS validator; enumerate registered HTTP routes and OpenAPI operations; compare identities and fail when any supported route lacks an operation, required parameter or schema, auth declaration, or response.

nodes.title: OpenAPI Generation
nodes.summary: Derive the OpenAPI artifact from authoritative code or schema sources and fail CI when regeneration differs from the committed or published specification. This prevents silent contract drift.
nodes.probe: Run the documented OpenAPI generation command in a clean checkout; compare the regenerated specification with the committed artifact; validate it with an OAS validator and fail on generation errors or unreviewed differences.

nodes.title: API Examples
nodes.summary: Provide minimal runnable workflows for authentication, valid requests, expected responses, sequencing, and representative failures. Practical examples turn a schema into a usable integration path.
nodes.probe: Extract API examples and run each against a local or mocked API target; assert status and response shape for success and representative failure cases and require safe placeholders for credentials and IDs.

nodes.title: API Behavior
nodes.summary: Document API semantics beyond schemas, including idempotency, pagination, ordering, retries, rate limits, consistency, and webhook delivery. Explicit behavior prevents unsafe client assumptions and retry amplification.
nodes.probe: Trace implementation, tests, gateway policy, and webhook workers against documented semantics; inspect evidence for retries, duplicate requests and events, pagination boundaries, ordering, rate limits, and eventual-consistency windows.

nodes.title: API Versioning
nodes.summary: Define supported API versions, compatibility guarantees, deprecation windows, sunset communication, and migration paths with examples. Consumers can plan upgrades instead of discovering breaking changes as outages.
nodes.probe: Compare the version support matrix with deployed routes, gateway configuration, response deprecation signals, release history, and migration docs; verify every advertised version has an owner, compatibility promise, and actionable sunset path.

nodes.title: Alert Runbook Links
nodes.summary: Attach a stable reachable runbook URL and matching alert identity to every actionable alert. Immediate diagnostic guidance reduces time to acknowledge and recover.
nodes.probe: Parse alert rules; for every actionable rule require a nonempty runbook URL, fetch it with failure-on-error and a timeout, and verify the runbook contains the exact alert identifier.

nodes.title: Runbook Procedure
nodes.summary: Make runbooks executable under pressure with impact, prerequisites, diagnostics, safe mitigations, verification, rollback, and stop conditions. Structured procedures reduce improvisation during high-cost failures.
nodes.probe: Execute the first diagnostic sequence in a safe environment and verify impact, prerequisites, commands, expected signals, mitigation, verification, rollback, and stop conditions are present and internally consistent.

nodes.title: Runbook Escalation
nodes.summary: Specify severity-based escalation contacts, ownership, incident-command expectations, vendor paths, and declaration or handoff criteria. Clear escalation prevents responders from losing time locating owners.
nodes.probe: Simulate each documented severity branch and verify contacts resolve, roles are unambiguous, vendor dependencies have escalation instructions, and handoff and declaration criteria are actionable.

nodes.title: Runbook Freshness
nodes.summary: Give every runbook an owner, review cadence, and update triggers for incidents and alert changes. Freshness checks catch retired commands, dashboards, owners, and alert identities before use.
nodes.probe: Parse runbook metadata; fail if owner is missing or the review interval is overdue; extract alert IDs and compare them with current alert definitions; resolve referenced URLs and report stale or missing dependencies.

nodes.title: Changelog Format
nodes.summary: Maintain a human-readable release-grouped changelog with user-relevant change types, newest releases first, and an Unreleased section. Links to authoritative release and migration references keep history useful.
nodes.probe: Inspect recent releases and the Unreleased section for consistent headings, user-visible entries, dates, and links; reconcile entries with release artifacts and known breaking or migration changes.

nodes.title: Changelog Gate
nodes.summary: Require every user-visible change to add a changelog entry or receive an explicit reviewable waiver during review. A change-aware gate prevents release-time sweeps from missing small breaking changes.
nodes.probe: Test the review workflow with a user-facing change and no changelog (expect failure), with a changelog entry (expect success), and with an authorized waiver (expect success plus recorded rationale).

nodes.title: Release Notes
nodes.summary: Explain each release's operational and user impact, fixes, breaking changes, migrations, limitations, upgrade steps, and complete changelog. This gives operators the information needed for safe adoption.
nodes.probe: Sample releases and cross-check notes against commits, changelog, migration scripts, and known limitations; verify required sections exist and upgrade steps are executable for affected deployment types.

nodes.title: Release Reproducibility
nodes.summary: Trace a published artifact from immutable source revision through toolchain, approvals, validation, checksums, and provenance, with deterministic rollback or yanking. Traceability enables containment and forensics when releases fail.
nodes.probe: Take a published release and trace source revision, build configuration, approvals, checksums or provenance, and validation evidence; dry-run rollback or yanking and identify a deterministic owner and command.

nodes.title: Contributing Guide
nodes.summary: Document setup, branch and commit conventions, tests and documentation checks, review preparation, and commands aligned with CI. Contributors get a complete path from change to merge without private process knowledge.
nodes.probe: Follow the guide in a clean checkout through setup, a small change, required checks, and pull-request preparation; verify every command exists, exits as documented, and matches CI configuration.

nodes.title: Documentation CODEOWNERS
nodes.summary: Assign reachable accountable reviewers to source, API schemas, diagrams, runbooks, and user documentation with explicit monorepo coverage. Ownership keeps documentation and operational guidance from silently decaying.
nodes.probe: Parse CODEOWNERS; for each required path resolve the effective owner and verify the owner exists and is reachable; test representative source, API, diagram, runbook, and documentation paths for coverage and precedence.

nodes.title: Pull Request Conventions
nodes.summary: Provide a concise pull-request checklist for scope, evidence, migration notes, screenshots, documentation impact, and reviewer responsibilities. Normalized review evidence exposes compatibility and operational consequences before merge.
nodes.probe: Inspect the pull-request template and sample merged requests, verifying the checklist requests required evidence and reviewers use it for code, API, migration, UI, and operational changes.

nodes.title: Documentation CI
nodes.summary: Build documentation in CI and validate navigation, links, includes, metadata, references, and generated pages before publication. Failing on unresolved content prevents defects from reaching users.
nodes.probe: Run `make docs-build`; `make docs-linkcheck`; and `make docs-validate`; assert each exits zero; scan generated output for unresolved-link markers, missing includes, malformed metadata, and placeholder tokens.

nodes.title: Documentation Example Tests
nodes.summary: Execute documentation code, commands, configuration fragments, and API examples or explicitly mark illustrative snippets as non-runnable. Testing supported versions keeps copy-paste guidance trustworthy.
nodes.probe: Run `make docs-examples-test`; enumerate fenced blocks and example scripts; execute every runnable item in an isolated environment; fail on nonzero status or expected-output drift and require an explicit marker on non-runnable snippets.

nodes.title: Documentation Navigation
nodes.summary: Organize documentation by user task and Diátaxis mode with reachable landing pages and no unintended orphan pages. Intentional navigation reduces unofficial duplicate guidance.
nodes.probe: Build the docs site and link graph; assert required landing pages are reachable from navigation; fail for broken links or pages with no inbound link except allowlisted index or generated pages.

nodes.title: Documentation Versioning
nodes.summary: Label version-sensitive documentation and distinguish current, archived, and end-of-life versions with immutable snapshots and migration links. Clear version boundaries prevent incompatible instructions from being applied.
nodes.probe: Select pages covering API, configuration, and migrations and verify version labels, selector behavior, support status, archive immutability, and migration links against deployed version-support policy.

nodes.title: Glossary
nodes.summary: Maintain concise authoritative definitions for terms, acronyms, states, and identifiers shared by code, APIs, alerts, and runbooks. Canonical vocabulary prevents contradictory automation and incident communication.
nodes.probe: Sample terms across code, API docs, alerts, and runbooks; verify each has one canonical definition and spelling and that cross-references resolve without contradicting contracts or state machines.

nodes.title: Support and Deprecation
nodes.summary: Document support channels, response expectations, supported versions, deprecation policy, security reporting, and feature or exception requests. Separate public support from private vulnerability reporting and make unsupported use visibly unsafe.
nodes.probe: Follow support, security, and deprecation links; verify channels are reachable and owned, supported versions match release policy, and a deprecated feature has notice, timeline, and migration instructions.

nodes.title: Issue Templates
nodes.summary: Collect environment, version, reproduction, expected and actual behavior, impact, and relevant logs while warning authors to redact secrets. Structured templates turn reports into triageable evidence without encouraging disclosure.
nodes.probe: For each `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*`, parse the template and require version, environment, reproduction, expected, actual, and impact fields plus a redaction warning; verify security issues route away from public templates.

nodes.title: Documentation Accessibility
nodes.summary: Render public documentation with semantic structure, meaningful alternatives, descriptive links, ordered headings, keyboard operation, focus states, and configured WCAG contrast. Accessible controls keep recovery and setup guidance usable by all readers.
nodes.probe: Build the documentation; run `pa11y --standard WCAG2AA --threshold 0 <published-or-local-docs-url>` or equivalent; fail on configured serious or critical violations and missing image alternatives, then manually verify keyboard navigation and focus on representative pages.
